rationale: The produced output file log/tab_ipw_mfgnmfg.scsv contains Table 7 with the change-in-average-log-wage coefficients on d_t~eusch_pw (Chinese import exposure per worker). Column (7) d_avg_l~_mfg is the manufacturing 'all workers' log-wage effect: coefficient 0.151 (SE 0.482), which is insignificant (t≈0.31) and matches the paper's 0.150 (SE 0.482). Column (10) d_avg_l~nmfg is the nonmanufacturing 'all workers' log-wage effect: coefficient -0.761 (SE 0.261), significant, matching the paper's -0.761 (SE 0.260). The corresponding Panel A employment-count effects also line up: column (1) lnchg_no_emp_mfg = -4.231 and column (4) lnchg_no_emp_nmfg = -0.274. All four target cells are within 5% relative error (mfg coef 0.151 vs 0.15, mfg SE 0.482 exact, nonmfg coef -0.761 exact, nonmfg SE 0.261 vs 0.260), so the claim that wage declines are concentrated outside manufacturing is fully supported.
